# Module guide: the grammar of movement

The slides follow the module in order, one slide per step. Open them beside the module, or run them on their own.

---

*Shadows: block:start*
## One ball, one floor, one second

This week you animate a ball that drops, bounces once and lands. The question to keep asking: what makes a ball look heavy?

---

*Shadows: block:first-pass*
## You go first

Five questions, before any explanation. Guess, commit, then read on. Nothing is scored, and you can redo any answer.

---

*Shadows: prompt:drop-chart*
## Prompt 1: the spacing chart

One column per drawing, 1 to 12. Height from 0 (the floor) to 10. It touches the floor on drawing 6, hops once, and lands on drawing 12. Even gaps look like an escalator.

![A spacing chart with twelve evenly spaced dots stepping down from 10 to 0](asset:spacing_how_to_read)

---

*Shadows: prompt:drawings-per-second*
## Prompt 2: pick a number

How many drawings for one second of film?

---

*Shadows: prompt:squash-keeps*
## Prompt 3: in your own words

The ball squashes. What stays the same?

---

*Shadows: prompt:before-leap*
## Prompt 4: think like the audience

Before a leap, what comes first?

---

*Shadows: prompt:heavy-light*
## Prompt 5: heavy or light

Same 24 frames, same start and stop. What differs?

---

*Shadows: block:lesson-spacing*
## Gaps grow as it falls

Close dots look slow, far dots look fast. The ball touches the floor on drawings 6 and 12. The ease is at the top of the hop, never at the floor.

![The reference bounce, one labeled dot per drawing](asset:spacing_reference_bounce)

---

*Shadows: block:lesson-ones-twos*
## 24 drawings, or 12

On ones: a new drawing every frame. On twos: each drawing held for two frames. Your ball is on twos: 12 drawings, 24 frames. Sound engineers picked 24 in 1926.

![On ones and on twos, the first half second](asset:ones_and_twos)

---

*Shadows: block:lesson-squash*
## The same amount of ball

Squash on contact, stretch in flight. Shorter means wider: the drawing's area stays about the same. On a contact drawing, the ball really touches the floor.

![Stretch, round, squash: shorter means wider](asset:squash_volume)

---

*Shadows: block:lesson-anticipation*
## Back first, then the action

A small move the opposite way shows the audience where to look. Written down in 1981 by Thomas and Johnston; worked out by a whole 1930s studio.

![A small move back, then a big arc forward](asset:anticipation)

---

*Shadows: block:lesson-timing*
## Same time, different places

Timing is how long. Spacing is where the ball is on each frame. Heavy: long eases. Light: short eases. Even: mechanical.

![Heavy, light and even spacing across the same 24 frames](asset:timing_vs_spacing)

---

*Shadows: block:examples*
## Check it against real life

A real ball, photographed 25 times a second. Compare the gaps near the floor with the gaps near the top.

![A stroboscopic photograph of a bouncing ball](asset:strobe_ball)

*Shadows: block:examples*
## Critique this one

Made to show off a file format, not weight. Name what is missing, in this week's words.

![A beach ball bouncing in a simple loop](asset:beach_ball_loop)

---

*Shadows: block:examples*
## It took a team

1878: a row of cameras, one frame at a time. Stanford paid, Muybridge staged it and patented the method, railroad engineers built the triggers, and the jockey G. Domm rode.

![The Horse in Motion, played as a loop](asset:horse_in_motion)

---

*Shadows: block:make*
## Your assignment

Your Prompt 1 chart, made to move. 12 drawings, each held two frames: drawing 1 on frame 1, drawing 6 on frame 11, drawing 12 on frame 23. Check the four sentences before handing in.

![From the chart's twelve drawings to the timeline's twenty-four frames](asset:chart_to_timeline)

---

*Shadows: prompt:plan-week*
## Your week

Two evenings, about 20 minutes each: the fall one night, the hop and landing the other. Name both evenings now. Sunday, play it back.

---

*Shadows: block:evening-fall*
## Evening one: the fall

Draw a floor line and a mark for 10 on the Fills layer; draw the ball on Lines. Put the bottom of the ball at each dot's height. Drawings 1 to 6. Only five minutes? Draw drawings 1 and 6.

---

*Shadows: block:evening-hop*
## Evening two: the hop

Drawings 7 to 12, landing on the floor. Play it three times. Floats? The gaps near the floor are too small. Save a video, or film your screen.

---

*Shadows: prompt:how-far*
## Sunday

Play it back. Say how far you got. Hand it in if you want feedback. There is never a grade.

---

*Shadows: block:second-pass*
## After you make it

The five questions again, from memory, beside your first answers.
